title: The Op-Amp That Tried to Output -10 V on ±5 V Rails
featured_title: THE OP-AMP THAT TRIED TO OUTPUT -10 V ON ±5 V RAILS
subject: electrical-computer
audience: FE Electrical and Computer candidates and engineering students

presentation.challenge: The gain equation requests -10 V, but the amplifier only has ±5 V rails.

practice.primary_question: Why can an inverting op amp with gain -2 fail to produce -10 V from a +5 V input?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using the ideal inverting-gain equation without checking whether the requested output is inside the supply/output limits.

case_dna.target_misconception: Using the ideal inverting-gain equation without checking whether the requested output is inside the supply/output limits.
case_dna.why_plausible: A familiar simplified electronics relation is easy to apply without checking the assumptions that make it valid.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: The ideal formula requests -10 V, but an op amp on ±5 V supplies cannot produce that linear output and saturates near the negative rail.
case_dna.corrected_model: Check the device model and operating region first, then apply the corresponding circuit equation.

problem_statement: An inverting op amp has R1 = 10 kΩ, Rf = 20 kΩ, Vin = +5 V, and ±5 V supplies. The ideal gain formula requests -10 V, but the real output cannot go beyond the negative supply limit and saturates.
fixed_constraints: Use the stated FE-style device model
Keep the stated source and main component values
